APPEAL No. 9015 of 2025  NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY
Versus  SMT. SUMAN AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Badri Nath Malhotra - learned Counsel for appell  Company.
Shri Akhilesh Kumar Gupta-learned Counsel for respond  Claimant.

 Shri Akhilesh Kumar Gupta-learned Counsel for respond  No.1- Claimant.

ORDER Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9015 of 2025 under Section 173(1) of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:216 2 MA-9015-2025 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the Insurance Company being dissatisfied with the award dated 18th August, 2025, passed by VIII Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 686 of 2024, whereby compensation of Rs. 11,33,300/- along with interest was awarded in National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30406624/
1 favour of claimant Smt. Suman against the Insurance Company, owner, and driver of the offending vehicle, jointly and severally, on account of permanent disability.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. Civil Revision No. 1210 of 2025 under Section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code has been filed against the same award dated 18th August, 2025, passed by the Claims Tribunal in Claim Case No.
687 of 2024, whereby compensation of Rs. 24,200/- along with interest was awarded in favour of claimant Bachhu Singh against the Insurance Company, owner, and driver of the offending vehicle,
jointly and severally, due to injuries sustained in the same motor accident on 18.02.2024.
3.
Since both matters arise from the same accident and involve common factual circumstances, they are heard together and a common order is passed.

4. The brief facts of the case are that on 18.02.2024, both claimants, Smt. Suman and her husband Bachhu Singh, were traveling on a motorcycle driven by Bachhu Singh as the rider, with Smt. Suman as pillion rider, towards Village Ratvai.

While passing opposite Krishi Farm, Police Thana Bijauli, a dumper truck bearing registration No. RJ05-GB-8085 (in short "offending vehicle"), coming from behind in a rash and negligent manner, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:216 3 MA-9015-2025 collided with the motorcycle.

As a result of the collision, Smt. Suman sustained grievous injuries, including crushing of her left foot, which necessitated amputation below the knee,
and injuries to other parts of her body.

She was initially admitted to District Hospital Morar,
subsequently transferred to Link Hospital, Gwalior, and later to Kalyani Hospital, Gwalior, where she remained hospitalized until 03.03.2024.

Bachhu Singh sustained injuries to his right foot,
femur, and other parts of his body.
The accident was reported to Police Station Bijauli.
5. Smt. Suman filed a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.48,00,000/-, including medical expenses, loss of earning, permanent disability, and future prospects.
Bachhu Singh filed a separate claim petition seeking compensation for injuries sustained in the same accident.
6. The owner and driver of the offending vehicle denied all allegations, including the occurrence of the accident.

The Insurance Company also submitted a written statement denying liability,
contending that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of Bachhu Singh on the motorcycle, that the motorcycle was overloaded, and that the insured vehicle was driven in violation of the insurance policy.
The Insurance Company prayed for dismissal of both claim petitions.

7. During the proceedings, the Claims Tribunal framed the necessary issues and recorded evidence,
including medical records, hospitalization documents, and statements of the claimants.
The Claims Tribunal rejected the Insurance Company's defense that the accident was caused solely by the claimants, and found that the insured vehicle was responsible.

The Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:216 4 MA-9015-2025 awarded Rs. 11,33,300/- to Smt. Suman, including compensation for permanent disability, loss of earning capacity, future prospects, and medical expenses, and compensation to the tune of Rs. 24,200/- awarded to Bachhu Singh.
8. The Insurance Company, being aggrieved, submitted that the Claims Tribunal erred in law and on facts on multiple grounds.

It was contended that the F.I.R. was filed after a delay of seven days National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30406624/
2 without any explanation, which casts doubt on the occurrence of the accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Insurance Company argued that the driver of the insured vehicle should have been summoned to give evidence under Order 16 Rule 1 of the Civil Procedure Code read with Section 169 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
and that the Tribunal's refusal to allow this application was unjust.

The Insurance Company also submitted that the accident occurred due to the negligence of Bachhu Singh, who drove the motorcycle rashly, carrying passengers in excess of capacity, and that the insured vehicle was not responsible.

It was further submitted that the loss of earning and permanent disability assessed in favour of Smt. Suman was not justified, as no doctor examined her specifically to determine loss of earning capacity, and that the compensation awarded was excessive.
The Insurance Company prayed that both awards be set aside and that it be exonerated from any liability as well as the amount which so deposited by the insurance company with interest be refunded.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants opposed the appeals, submitting that the Claims Tribunal correctly examined all evidence on record, including the police report, medical documents, hospitalization NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:216 5 MA-9015-2025 records, and statements of the claimants.
It was argued that the Insurance Company failed to prove contributory negligence on the part of the claimants, or that the accident did not occur as alleged.

It was further submitted that the Tribunal acted in accordance with the settled principles of law relating to motor accident claims in assessing compensation for permanent disability, loss of earning capacity, and medical expenses.
10. Heard learned Counsel for the parties.

Perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.11.
11.
Upon perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the accident occurred on 18.02.2024.

From Ex.P-76, it is evident that Smt. Suman (claimant), along with her husband Bachhu (claimant), initially went to Morar Hospital where pre-MLC was conducted, and thereafter Smt. Suman was referred for higher treatment.
On perusal of the Medico-Legal Report Ex.P-11, it is found that Smt. Suman was admitted to Link Hospital, Gwalior, on 19.02.2024.
A bare reading of Ex.P-76 and Ex.P-11 clearly establishes that a road accident had occurred.
After completion of treatment, the husband of Smt. Suman, namely Bachhu, lodged the FIR regarding the alleged accident on 25.02.2024.
12. It is true that if the claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for delay in lodging the FIR, such delay should not be treated as fatal to the proceedings.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others, AIR 2011 SC 1226 , in paragraphs 20 and 21, has held as under:
"20.

entities.text: Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others, AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the c l a i m a n t ' s c a s e .

K n o w i n g t h e I n d i a n N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2026:MPHC-GWL:216 6 MA-9015-2025 conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.

Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30406624/
3 mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

13. So far as the contention of the appellant that the accident was caused by the driver of the motorcycle and not by the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned, on perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the FIR was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle and, after investigation, the police filed a charge-sheet against him.

It is a settled principle of law that when a charge-sheet is filed against the driver of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:216 7 MA-9015-2025 the offending vehicle, the Claims Tribunal can presume negligence on his part, subject to rebuttal.

14. Mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be treated as fatal to the case of the claimant, especially when a satisfactory explanation has been furnished and the accident itself stands proved by cogent evidence.
The presumption arising from filing of the charge-sheet is rebuttable; however, the burden to rebut such presumption lies upon the person alleging false implication.

In the present case,
neither the driver nor the owner of the offending vehicle entered the witness box to rebut the evidence of the claimants or the eye-witness.
15. The Claims Tribunal has acted in accordance with law and has correctly assessed the compensation on the basis of evidence available on record.
The delay in filing the FIR and the plea of contributory negligence were duly considered and found insufficient to dislodge the claim of the claimants.

16. As regards the contention of the appellant that an application was filed to summon the driver of the offending vehicle to rebut the criminal documents, upon perusal of the order-sheet dated 30.07.2025, it is evident that the Claims Tribunal rightly rejected the application filed under Order National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30406624/
4 16 Rule 1 CPC.

entities.text: Order National Insurance Company Limited vs Bachhu Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No prejudice has been caused to the appellant by such rejection.

17. In view of the aforesaid discussion, it is clear that although a case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, he did not enter the witness box to rebut the criminal documents or the evidence led by the claimants.
Therefore, the Claims Tribunal has rightly held the driver of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:216 8 MA-9015-2025 offending vehicle responsible for the accident.

18. With regard to the contention of the appellant regarding non- examination of the doctor to prove permanent disability, upon perusal of the medical documents on record, it is evident that respondent No.1/claimant Smt. Suman sustained grievous injuries, including crushing of her left foot, necessitating amputation below the knee, along with injuries to other parts of her body.
In such circumstances, examination of the doctor was not essential to establish permanent disability.
The Tribunal has rightly held that Smt. Suman suffered permanent disability due to the accident.
The application under Order 16 Rule 1 CPC read with Section 169 of the Motor Vehicles Act was rejected by a reasoned order, which does not suffer from perversity.

19. The Claims Tribunal has meticulously examined the medical documents, police papers,
statements of the claimants, and other material available on record.
The defence of the Insurance Company, including the plea of contributory negligence and delay in lodging the FIR, was duly considered and rightly rejected.
20. The Tribunal has correctly applied the principles under Sections 166 and 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The Insurance Company has failed to establish that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the motorcycle driver.

The Tribunal rightly assessed compensation considering the medical evidence, hospitalization records, age and nature of disability suffered by the claimant- Smt. Suman as well as nature of injuries sustained by claimant- Bachhu.
21.

In view of the foregoing discussion and settled legal principles, no NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:216 9 MA-9015-2025 merit is found in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9015 of 2025 filed by the Insurance Company or in Civil Revision No. 1210 of 2025.
Accordingly, both the Miscellaneous Appeal and the Civil Revision are dismissed.
The common award dated 18.08.2025 passed by the Claims Tribunal in Claim Case Nos. 686 and 687 of 2024 is hereby upheld.
No order as to costs.
22. A copy of this order be placed on record of the connected Civil Revision No. 1210 of 2025.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
